xBRIEFInfo.description: Story xBRIEF for #3650 canonical consumer-hard-blocker label; bound after a single-critic arc refuted the title-token proposal.

plan.title: feat(scm,guidance): one canonical consumer-hard-blocker label, not a title token

narratives.Description: No canonical label means 'a Directive consumer cannot complete an intended flow and has no reasonable workaround'. adoption-blocker is scoped to onboarding and first session by its own wording, Upgrade Blocker is upgrade-specific, status:blocked means this issue waits on something else, and urgent has drifted into broad priority across eleven open issues. So a consumer hard stop at update, task check, or ship has no home. This story defines one canonical label with positive-only semantics and reviewable classification evidence.
narratives.Overview: The original proposal -- require a BLOCKER token in issue titles -- was REFUTED by its critic and is withdrawn. Do not implement a title token, and do not implement a title linter. The arc established that triage:queue ranks exclusively by labels, that gh issue list and the queue renderer both already display labels, and that ten open issues already carry BLOCKER titles in a form contradicting the original proposal with eight of them unlabeled. Those ten are #3699's problem, not this story's.
narratives.Labels: documentation, enhancement, agent-experience, process, scm, urgent, area:guidance, design-critique:triage-ready
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer triaging a consumer hard stop, I want one canonical label whose definition covers the whole intended-flow range, so that the ranking queue surfaces it and I am not forced to choose between a too-narrow label and a priority label that means something else.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Decide the label. Prefer BROADENING adoption-blocker to 'consumer cannot complete an intended Directive flow without a reasonable workaround' if its onboarding-specific meaning need not be preserved; otherwise add one canonical ranking label through the normal taxonomy process. Record which was chosen and why. 2. Ensure the definition covers the full range named in the issue: install, first session, update, task check, ship. 3. State the classification test and the required body evidence in content/scm/github.md Issue Workflow -- affected consumer flow and version, documented alternatives attempted, observed recovery cost, triage owner and date. 4. State the positive-only semantics explicitly and prominently: the label means classified as a blocker; its absence means NOT CLASSIFIED, never 'a workaround exists'. 5. Update .github/ISSUE_LABELS.md so the label is distinguished from Upgrade Blocker, status:blocked and urgent. 6. Confirm the label is present in ranking configuration and displays on triage:queue rows -- the renderer already prints the matched ranking label, so verify rather than build. 7. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] line.
narratives.LockedDecisions: The BLOCKER title token is WITHDRAWN in any form -- refuted as a fifth parallel authoritative signal. Reasons, all measured: triage:queue ranks only labels; gh issue list and the queue renderer both display labels already; title and label are independently mutable and can disagree while the queue trusts one; a title is filer-controlled untrusted content whereas a label is taxonomy state applied or confirmed by triage; and absence of an unenforced token cannot be made informative, because a negative inference does not degrade gracefully the way a positive cue does. A fail-closed title linter is also rejected -- it would need authority rules, exceptions, recut handling and label synchronization, which is a second state machine around data already modelled as labels. Do NOT substitute urgent; the open set shows it is broad priority and this issue is itself urgent while explicitly not being a blocker. This story OVERRIDES the original non-goal 'inventing a new BLOCKER GitHub label' -- recorded deliberately, because the taxonomy gap is real and a parallel channel is the wrong way to close it. Out of scope: relabeling the ten existing BLOCKER-titled issues (#3699), rewriting historical titles, and building for Slack or any other title-only integration before one is measured to exist and to be unable to display labels.
narratives.AcceptanceJustification: Eight clauses from the recut issue checklist. The ranking and display clause is verify-only because the renderer already prints the matched ranking label.
